title: Failure probability of the Fourier estimator
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2]$. Suppose the total squared Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$. Then the probability that the estimator with parameters $\mathcal F,\varepsilon,\delta$ outputs a hypothesis whose relative Hamming distance from $f$ is strictly greater than $\varepsilon$ is at most $\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$\mathcal F$ is a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
$\varepsilon,\delta$ belong to the stated positive learning-parameter interval
The squared Fourier weight of $f$ outside $\mathcal F$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$
